newsitem.title: UK: UK to overhaul radio spectrum pricing.
newsitem.headline: UK to overhaul radio spectrum pricing.

text.p: The government said on Wednesday it hoped to find time in the next 18 months to pass a bill that would charge competitive prices for the use of Britain's radio spectrum.

It said the use of radio by a wide range of businesses, from taxi companies to broadcasters and phone operators, contributed an estimated 12 billion pounds to Britain's gross domestic product and was growing at one billion pounds a year.
But with spectrum shortages already apparent, the government said future growth depended critically on the effective management of the airways.
Under current legislation, charges for radio licences are based on the administrative costs of the Radiocommunications Agency rather than the economic value of the spectrum.
Users thus have no incentive to maximise spectrum efficiency, and hoarding of licences is encouraged.

The government's proposals would break the link between licence fees and spectrum mangement costs, enabling fees, which would be set by secondary legislation, to reflect more closely the value of the spectrum.
Higher charges would, however, be limited to those services and parts of the country where there is already congestion. Around 80 percent of licensees are expected to pay no more than at present.
The bill would also provide for:
-- financial assistance to be given to users, to reinforce the effects of spectrum pricing.
-- additional security of tenure for users.
